steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this step by step:

Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Six days from today would be Friday, October 30, 2026.

The deadline is Friday, October 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT (Pacific Time).

Spain (Madrid) is in the Central European Time (CET/CEST) zone. In October, Spain is on CET (UTC+1). Pacific Time (PT) is UTC-7 in October (PDT).

The time difference is 8 hours, with Spain being ahead of Pacific Time.

11:59 PM PT = 7:59 AM the next day in Madrid (CET)

So the deadline of Friday, October 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT becomes Saturday, October 31, 2026 at 7:59 AM CET.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this step by step:

- Today is Friday, October 30, 2026
- The deadline is "this coming Monday" at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time
- This coming Monday would be November 2, 2026
- Los Angeles is in the Pacific Time zone (PT)
- Madrid is in the Central European Time zone (CET/CEST)
- In November, Los Angeles is on PST (UTC-8) and Madrid is on CET (UTC+1)
- This means Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles

When it's 10:00 AM in Los Angeles, it's 7:00 PM (19:00) in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts on Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours.

48 hours is exactly 2 days. So I need to add 2 days to the start date and time.

Start: Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00
End: Monday, October 26, 2026 at 18:00

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this step by step:

1. The contest starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT (Pacific Time)
2. Submissions close 72 hours later, which is exactly 3 days
3. So submissions close on October 29, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT
4. Madrid, Spain is in Central European Time (CET/CEST)
5. During October, Spain is on CEST (UTC+2) while Pacific Time is PDT (UTC-7)
6. This means Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Pacific Time
7. So when it's 10:00 AM PT on October 29, 2026, it's 7:00 PM (19:00) CEST on the same date in Madrid

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this step by step:

1. Submissions close: October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (Eastern Time)
2. Results are announced 36 hours later
3. Madrid, Spain is in Central European Time (CET/CEST)

First, I'll convert the submission closing time to Madrid time:
- ET (Eastern Time) is UTC-5 (or UTC-4 during DST)
- Madrid (CET) is UTC+1, which is 6 hours ahead of ET

So 11:59 PM ET = 5:59 AM the next day in Madrid

Adding 36 hours to October 31, 2026 at 5:59 AM Madrid time:
- 36 hours = 1 day and 12 hours
- This brings us to November 1, 2026 at 5:59 PM + 12 hours = November 2, 2026 at 5:59 AM

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 05:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert the Unix timestamp 1791788340 to Tokyo local time.

Unix timestamps are in UTC, so I'll first convert this to UTC time, then adjust for Tokyo's timezone (UTC+9).

1791788340 corresponds to:
- UTC time: 2026-08-10 17:59:00 UTC
- Tokyo time: 2026-08-11 02:59:00 (UTC+9)

ANSWER: 2026-08-11 02:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is given in UTC (Zulu time). Madrid, Spain is in the Central European Time (CET/CEST) zone, which is UTC+1 in winter and UTC+2 in summer.

Since October 25, 2026 falls during the transition period from summer to winter time, I need to check if daylight saving time is still active. In Spain, daylight saving time ends on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026 itself. 

On this date, Spain will still be on CEST (UTC+2) until the transition occurs, but since the UTC time is 02:30Z, and Spain would be at 04:30 CEST, the transition to CET (UTC+1) would happen later that day.

Therefore, the deadline of 02:30 UTC on October 25, 2026 corresponds to 04:30 CEST in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 04:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Pacific Time (PT) to Madrid time for the last Sunday of October 2026.

First, let me identify the date: the last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25, 2026.

For time zones: 
- Pacific Time (PT) is UTC-7 during daylight saving time
- Madrid is in Central European Time (CET/CEST), which is UTC+2 during daylight saving time

The time difference is 9 hours (Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Pacific Time).

11:59 PM Pacific Time = 23:59 PT
Adding 9 hours: 23:59 + 9 hours = 08:59 the next day

So 11:59 PM on October 25, 2026 Pacific Time = 08:59 AM on October 26, 2026 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 08:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find when the US ends daylight saving time in 2026, then convert that to Lima, Peru time.

The US typically ends daylight saving time on the first Sunday in November. In 2026, this will be November 1st.

On November 1, 2026:
- The US will be on Eastern Standard Time (EST), which is UTC-5
- Lima, Peru is on Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5 year-round

So when it's 12:00 noon Eastern Time in the US, it will also be 12:00 noon in Lima, Peru, since both are in the same time zone (UTC-5).

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) means the deadline is when it's 24:00 (midnight) on December 31, 2026, anywhere on Earth. This effectively means the latest possible time zone, which is UTC+14 (Line Islands, Kiribati).

Tokyo is UTC+9, so I need to convert from UTC+14 to UTC+9.
UTC+14 at 24:00 on December 31, 2026 is the same as UTC+9 at 19:00 on December 31, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-12-31 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Sydney time to Madrid time for the deadline of 5:00 PM on October 5, 2026.

Sydney, Australia (AEDT) is UTC+11
Madrid, Spain (CEST) is UTC+2

The time difference is 9 hours, with Sydney being 9 hours ahead of Madrid.

So 5:00 PM in Sydney = 8:00 AM in Madrid (subtracting 9 hours).

Since this is on October 5, 2026, and both locations will still be on their respective daylight saving time schedules at that point, the conversion is straightforward.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 08:00
